digest.component_or_area: rebar.llm.evals.provider_parity — bedrock vs anthropic parity measurement harness
propositions: Bedrock inference-profile IDs fail parity bar at standard slot with 1 decision-level flip on gold set (must be 0) and at frontier slot with 2 flips, verdict agreement 0.929 < 0.95 floor, and false-accept criterion rise of 0.143 > 0.02 margin.

Paired corpus run over 28 gold items across both class slots (standard and frontier) with N=3 epochs per arm shows all three observed decision flips favor Bedrock accuracy, with structured-output validity at 1.000 on both providers and zero runtime errors.

The harness harnesses gate_config scope to ensure provider is the only variable between v1 (direct Anthropic) and v2 (Bedrock) arms, with usage-log attestation showing zero non-Bedrock calls on v2 arm and confirmed split-brain prevention via context-variable copying under concurrency.

Bedrock latency is at or better parity than direct Anthropic (standard 9.9% faster, frontier within 0.1%), settling earlier N=1 pilot hint of 35% slowdown; temperature=0 override for opus-4-8 confirmed working in practice with zero sampling-parameter rejections.

Anthropic-vs-Anthropic noise-floor control run not approved; without it cannot confirm whether zero decision-level flips criterion is achievable by any provider pair, making bar confirmation dependent on root-cause fixes to 62ac (false-accept metric inverted) and 635f (errored pairs scored as flips) then offline re-score of recorded results.
